lines.jp:
信天翁号は飛び立った。
　
　海流渦巻いて流れ落ちるその中心へ。
　要らぬものどもを突き落とす、この世界の排泄口の中を、飛ぶ。
　この世界に必要だった、悪意の受け皿として望まれた信天翁号が。
　くそったれと叫んで、自ら望んで飛び込んだのだ。
lines.en:
The Albatross took flight. 

Into the center where currents spiraled and poured away. 
She flew inside this world's sewer, the hole down which it cast everything it did not need. 
The Albatross, whom this world had needed and desired as a receptacle for its malice-- 
shouted, 'Damn you all,' and plunged in because she chose to.

lines.jp:
古来、世界に果てを造った者はみな、そこに嵐と、落ちれば二度と上がってはこれない深い穴を置く。
　切り立つ断崖絶壁では、人は希望を込めてよじ登ろうとしてしまうから、永遠に落ち続ける果てを造るのだ。
lines.en:
Since ancient times, all who made an end for a world placed there a storm and a hole so deep that anything fallen in could never climb out again. 
A sheer cliff invites a human being to climb it in hope. And so they make an end through which one falls forever.

lines.jp:
しかし、今、信天翁号は飛ぶ。
　三本のマストに張られたその帆に風をはらみ。
　陸地の見えぬ海原をいつまででも飛び続ける信天翁。
lines.en:
But now the Albatross flew. 
Wind filled the sails spread upon her three masts. 
An albatross that could fly forever above a sea with no land in sight.

lines.jp:
そう、飛び続けるのだ、飛び続けていられるのだ。
　どこまで落ちようとも。
　いつか必ず、羽根休められる場所を見つけるまでは。
lines.en:
Yes. She would keep flying. She could keep flying. 
No matter how far she fell. 
Until the day she found a place where her wings might rest.

lines.jp:
嵐にまかれて羽根は折れ、その体傷つけられても。
　帆は破れ、マストは折れ、ついにその船体すら粉々に。
　乗り組みどもをぶちまけながらも。
lines.en:
Though the storm caught her, broke her wings, and wounded her body. 
Though sails tore, masts snapped, and at last the hull itself shattered to pieces. 
Though she spilled her crew into the void as she went.

lines.jp:
ああ、信天翁。
　
　
　お前はきっと見つけられる。
　お前はきっと辿り着ける。
　
　
　そこに───
　その場所に───
lines.en:
Ah, Albatross. 


Surely you will find it. 
Surely you will arrive. 


There-- 
in that place--

lines.jp: それは、彼が知る祖国と、同じようでいてどこか異なる景色だった。
lines.en: It was a landscape at once like the homeland he knew and somehow unlike it.

lines.jp: その国はついこの間、敗北を受け入れたばかりだった。世界中を巻き込んだ大戦の最後の敗者となることを。
lines.en: Only a short while earlier, that nation had accepted defeat--accepted that it was the last loser in the great war that had engulfed the world.

lines.jp: 空から街を焼かれ、海外に持つ領土をすべて失い、因業の炎の二柱、たくさんの民が死に、兵は殺し殺され、そしてやっと敗北の宣言読み上げて、戦争を終わらせたばかりだった。
lines.en: Its cities had been burned from the sky. Every territory overseas was lost. Two pillars of karmic flame had risen. A great many civilians died; soldiers killed and were killed. Only then was the declaration of defeat read aloud, bringing the war to an end.

lines.jp: その時、この国民はなにを思っただろう。悔しさか、悲しみか、あるいは安堵か。ともかく張り詰めていたものが切れ、誰もが一度膝をついたのだった。
lines.en: What did the people of that country think in that hour? Bitterness? Grief? Or perhaps relief? Whatever had been stretched taut within them snapped, and every person sank once to their knees.

lines.jp: しかし、彼らは次の日には立ち上がる。残されたのは焼き払われ荒廃した国土であっても、生きてゆかねばならぬのだから。立ち上がり廃材集めて家を作り、土くれを鋤で打ち、生きる術を探し出す。混乱はまだしばらく続こうとも、彼らは足を踏み出した。皆が前を向いて進むのなら、その息吹はこの国に、復興という風を吹かせる。そんな時代だった。
lines.en: Yet on the following day they stood. Burned and ruined land might be all that remained, but they had to live. They rose, gathered wreckage and made houses, struck clotted earth with hoes, and hunted out the means of survival. Confusion would continue for some time, but they stepped forward. If everyone advanced facing ahead, their breath would make a wind called reconstruction blow across the nation. Such was the age.

lines.jp:
そこに彼は辿り着いた。
　どこからとは言わぬ。
　どうやってとも言わぬ。
lines.en:
There he arrived. 
From where, no telling. 
How, no telling.

lines.jp: ただ、遥か遠い異国の地で海に投げ入れられた空き瓶が海流に乗って砂浜に流れ着いたように襤褸屑同然の格好で、ここに辿り着いたのだ。
lines.en: He reached this place looking no better than a bundle of rags--like an empty bottle thrown into the sea in some far foreign land, borne upon the current, and washed onto the sand.

lines.jp: 放っておけばそこでそのまま死体となっていたかもしれぬほど、疲れ果て動けずにいた彼は幸いな事に拾われる。
lines.en: He lay exhausted beyond movement, near enough to becoming a corpse if left there. By good fortune, someone picked him up.

lines.jp: 彼を拾ったのは、街の片隅で身を寄せ合って巣を作り、街駆け巡って日々の糧をあらゆる手使って稼ぐ、浮浪児達だった。戦争の中、あるいはその後の混乱の中、死に別れたかはぐれたか或いは故あって放り出されたか、親も失く庇護者もいない子供達だった。
lines.en: The ones who picked him up were street children. They huddled together in a nest in one corner of the city and raced its streets, using every means they possessed to earn each day's food. Some had lost their parents to death or separation during the war or the confusion after it; others had been cast away for reasons of their own. They were children with neither parent nor protector.

lines.jp: 倒れた彼を見つけた浮浪児達は、野垂れ死にの体から金目のものでも毟って埋めてやろうと近づいてみれば、まだ息のあることに驚いた。彼らは顔突き合わせ、何を相談しどうまとまったのかはわからぬが、その行き倒れを自分達の住み処まで、彼の手持ち足持ちやや扱いは雑ながら、引きずっていった。そして、多くはないが、幸運な事に仲間の一人が今日は大当たり引き当てたのが幸いした、食べ物と水を分け与えた。
lines.en: The street children had approached the fallen man intending to tear anything valuable from a body dead by the roadside and then give it burial. They were astonished to find him breathing. They put their heads together. Whatever they discussed and however agreement emerged, in the end they seized the castaway by arms and legs and dragged him to their den with less than perfect gentleness. Their supplies were meager. Luckily, one of their number had struck a tremendous success that day, and so they shared food and water.

lines.jp: 浮浪児達にしてみれば、大人の一人も仲間にいれば、いろいろと便利もあるだろうと考えたのかもしれぬ。気まぐれが入り込んでいたことは大いに否定できぬ。なぁに、厄介となれば追い出してしまえばいいとはやや浅慮ともいえるが。しかし、自分達の身の上多少は顧みれば捨て置く事が出来なかったのだとすれば、小狡く生き抜く彼らの中にも、純心は汚れず残っているのだろう。それは拾われた男にとっても、浮浪児達にとっても、この国の行く末にとっても幸いであるに違いない。
lines.en: Perhaps the street children reasoned that having one adult among their number might prove useful. Whim had surely entered the decision as well. 'If he becomes trouble, throw him out' was not the most farsighted plan. Yet if some recollection of their own circumstances made them unable to leave him there, then unstained innocence still survived inside these cunning little experts at staying alive. That must have been fortunate for the man they picked up, for the children, and for the future of this nation alike.

lines.jp:
明けて翌朝まだ早く。
　ものすごい勢いで与えた食べ物平らげたかと思ったら、また倒れて眠り込んだ昨日からの居候を、浮浪児達、その頭蹴り飛ばして手荒く起こす。せっかく拾ったからには、働いてもらわねば困るのだ。動ける者に無駄飯食わせる余裕はなし、稼ぎが悪けりゃ飯抜きだ、それでも悪けりゃ追い出すぞと脅して彼を住み処から引っ張り出す。
lines.en:
Early the next morning-- 
the street children woke yesterday's new lodger roughly by kicking him in the head. He had devoured their food with astonishing speed, then collapsed and slept again. If they had gone to the trouble of picking him up, they needed him to work. They had no room to waste food on anyone capable of moving. Earn badly and go hungry; keep earning badly and be thrown out. Threatening him with these terms, they hauled him from the den.

lines.jp:
向かう先は荒廃の混乱から自然発生した物流の集積地、闇市だった。
　前年の挑発から隠し通した米の余り、庭先の土掘り起こしてようやく実った野菜、配給切り詰めて貯めた小麦粉などの食料品から、それを焼いたり捌いたり欠けた椀に鍋の中味よそって出すもあり、焼失免れた家屋の箪笥から引っ張り出した衣類、同様になんとか守り通した本雑誌しかしこちらはやや人気薄か、そして出所問えぬ品々等々、ある者は金に困り、ある者は物に困り、ある者は目聡く金儲けの機会狙って集い来る。
lines.en:
Their destination was a gathering place for goods that had sprung spontaneously from ruin and confusion: the black market. 
There was rice hidden through the previous year's levy; vegetables finally coaxed from earth dug up in front gardens; flour saved by shaving portions from rations. Some stalls cooked or carved up those foods, or ladled the contents of pots into chipped bowls. Clothes had been hauled from dressers in houses spared by fire; books and magazines had somehow survived as well, though interest in those was thin; and there were goods whose origins no one asked. Some came desperate for money, others desperate for things, and still others with eyes sharp for profit.

lines.jp: 商品抱えた者どもが思い思いに店を広げて連なり通りの左右を埋め尽くす。そこに品求めて人が集まるのだから、そこは常にごった返して喧噪もやかましい。そして、こんな場所だから糧を稼ぐ、まぁどのようにかは聞かぬとして、機会も多かろうと浮浪児達は男を連れてきたのだ。お前はでかいんだから、自分達とは別のやりようもあるんだろうと言いながら。
lines.en: People bearing merchandise spread shops wherever they pleased until both sides of the street were full. Buyers gathered in pursuit of goods, so the place remained a crush of bodies and noise. The children had brought the man because a place like this must offer many chances to earn food--though how, precisely, we shall not ask. You are big, they told him. You must have ways we do not.

lines.jp: 男への案内もそこそこに、浮浪児達は稼ぎ求めて散っていく。
lines.en: After a brief introduction, the street children scattered in search of earnings.

lines.jp:
残された男と言えば……、まぁ、人混みの中で立ち尽くし、呆然としていたわけだ。
　右も左もわからぬ彼にとっては異国の地。稼げと言われてもどうしたものやら。この手には技も何もありはしないのだ。一宿一飯の恩はありがたいが、さてどう報いたものか、いや待て、このままとんずらこいてもかまわんのじゃないかなぁ、などと。
lines.en:
As for the man left behind... well, he stood vacant and motionless within the crowd. 
To him it was foreign country: he knew neither right from left nor one custom from another. Told to earn, what could he possibly do? These hands possessed no craft at all. He was grateful for a night's shelter and a meal, but how could he repay them? Then again, wait--perhaps there was nothing wrong with running off as he was...

lines.jp: ぼんやりと休んだがましの考え巡らせながら、眺めていた人混みの中に。
lines.en: While such faintly better-than-worthless thoughts wandered through his vacant head, within the crowd he watched--

lines.jp: いたのだ。
lines.en: She was there.

lines.jp: あの時と同じように。
lines.en: Just as she had been then.

lines.jp: 濃緑が光の加減でわずかに覗く黒髪を、風にまるで翼はためかすように遊ばせる、雑踏の中をすいすいと、人の流れを気流に見立てたかのようにその合間を自在に縫って。
lines.en: Black hair, showing deep green only where the light found it, played in the wind like beating wings. She slipped through the throng, threading every gap as freely as though the current of people were a current of air.

lines.jp:
男、思わず駆け出す。
　こちらは、人にぶつかり物にぶつかり、舌打ちとまれに怒号をかけられながら、近づいていく。
　その背があとわずかまでとよろめき出たところで、男は何かを叫んだだろうか。あるいは何も言わずに立ち尽くしただろうか。どちらを選んだのだとしても。
lines.en:
The man broke into a run without thinking. 
He, unlike her, collided with people and goods and drew clicks of the tongue and an occasional angry shout as he closed the distance. 
When he stumbled to within a few steps of her back, did the man cry something out? Or did he stop without a word? Whichever he chose--

lines.jp: 少女は振り返る。ごく自然に。すぐ後ろに男がいて、自分を見つめているのが当たり前であるというように。
lines.en: the young woman turned. Perfectly naturally--as though of course the man would be standing directly behind her, looking at her.

lines.jp:
「───また、海に出よう、直正。
　今度こそ、本当の海だよ。
　みんなが待っているから」
lines.en:
'--Let us go to sea again, Naomasa. 
This time, to the true sea. 
Everyone is waiting.'

lines.jp:
「そして、誰よりも。なによりも。
　私が待っているから。
　航海は、まだ───終わらない」
lines.en:
'And more than anyone. More than anything. 
I am waiting. 
The voyage is not--over yet.'

lines.jp: 「君の望む限り───」
lines.en: 'For as long as you desire--'

lines.jp:
『巻末劇』
　
　
「たのむ、いってくれ、トラップ」
　
「ふりかえってあんたの姿を見たら、
　前みたいにまた神経衰弱を起こす……
　たのむよ、トラップ」
　
　
「そういうときにゃよう、
　ミスター、
　海に出て元気を取り戻すのが一番だぜ」
　
　
　　　　　　　　　　　ある船員の会話
　
　　　　───信天翁航海録───
　　　了
lines.en:
'Endpiece'


'Please, go away, Trapp.'

'If I turn around and see you, 
I'll suffer another nervous collapse like the one before... 
Please, Trapp.'


'At times like that, 
mister, 
the best thing is to put to sea and recover your spirits.'


　　　　　　　　　　　A Conversation Between Sailors

　　　　--Albatross Koukairoku--
　　　The End
